properties.title: Per-owner push bound; last push carries max feed_seq
Durable writes equal N; durable state byte-identical to the bare path
Reader never ends below the latest committed feed_seq
Monotonic announced position; no regressive push on the wire
Per-owner isolation across interleaved multi-owner workloads
Coalescing is idempotent on a quiesced owner
Fail-safe never costs durability or freshness
Window bound derives from the authority; over-long window refused
Push count independent of worker and request count

microbenchmark.cpu_ms_shape_proxy: per-push shape in the R2-23 baseline units (+2.3 CPU-ms / 72 pushes); NOT a wall-clock measurement

verification_obligation.detail: one PUBLISH per write/batch; AST tripwire that no serving package reaches the write-side publish surface; push count a function of W and O only, invariant to simulated N and R

deferred_cloud_gates: Knee_Re_Measure (Req 9): fleet-scale push-cost re-measurement at the capacity knee (36 workers / real Valkey / real request load). OPEN. The microbenchmark is its local representative and does not close it.
known_findings: The per-request/per-worker 72-pushes defect is already closed by GW05c; R2-23 verifies it (Req 1 tripwire), it does not re-fix it.
Two test-harness bugs (counting the window-close catch-up as an in-window push) were found and fixed in the tests; no product bug, no property weakened.
